2.title: Health Equity in Beta Cell Therapies

history.reason: Owner ruling 2026-10-06: Gap #2 is the specific question 'Health Equity in Beta Cell Therapies', rated claim by claim (owner: 'be as specific as possible'). Claim profile 0% GOLD / 20% SILVER / 80% BRONZE / 0% unverified; headline = the median claim's tier.

claims.claim: No published analysis or registered study examines who can get stem-cell or islet replacement therapy for type 1 diabetes, by country income, race or insurance.
sources: PubMed, all time, searched 2026-10-06: 34 hits, none an access or equity analysis (query in gap2_null_searches.json)
ClinicalTrials.gov, searched 2026-10-06: 32 studies, none on access to cell therapy (query in gap2_null_searches.json)
claims.scope: PubMed-indexed papers and registered studies only; Embase and conference abstracts not searched.
adjacent: PMID:31127682 (bioprocess economics of stem cell therapies for T1D, 2019)

claims.claim: The two trials of zimislecel, the most advanced stem cell-derived islet product, list 36 sites in 10 countries, all high-income.
Of 76 active type 1 diabetes islet, stem-cell or beta-cell studies with listed sites, none has a site in India or in any African country.
About a fifth of people with type 1 diabetes live in low- and lower-middle-income countries: 1.8 million of 8.4 million in 2021, 2.1 million of 9.5 million in 2025.
sources: PMID:40412624 (IDF Atlas 11th ed / T1D Index v3, 2025)
claims.note: Two editions of one model, so one source.

claims.claim: Remaining life expectancy for a child diagnosed at 10 differs by country income: 13 years in low-income versus 65 in high-income countries (2021).
